title: Financial Analyst
one_line: The standard first finance job. Builds the numbers other people decide with.
what_they_do: Prepares forecasts, budgets, variance analysis and management reporting. Owns the models that tell a business what happened and what is likely to happen next. Most of the work is in Excel, and most of the value is in noticing what the number implies.
typical_week: Update a monthly forecast and explain the variance
Build or fix a model somebody else started
Reconcile two reports that should agree and do not
Prepare a management pack for review
Answer 'why is this number different from last month'
what_it_is_not: Not accounting. Accountants record what happened; analysts explain it and project forward.
skills_must: Explaining a number in plain words
entry_paths: B.Com or BBA with strong Excel
whats_hard: You are asked for certainty about a future nobody can know, and blamed when the forecast is wrong.
not_for_you_if: You dislike being questioned about your assumptions. Every number you produce will be challenged.
demand_note: Very high volume in India across corporates, GCCs and startups. The default destination for PGDM Finance graduates.

title: FP&A Analyst
one_line: Forecasting and business planning — the finance seat closest to actual decisions.
what_they_do: Owns the planning cycle: annual budget, rolling forecast, and the business review that follows. Partners with department heads rather than serving them, and is expected to challenge a plan that does not add up.
typical_week: Run the forecast cycle and chase inputs from business owners
Build a driver-based model rather than a spreadsheet of assumptions
Prepare the monthly business review deck
Challenge a department's headcount request with numbers
Model a scenario leadership asked about on a call
what_it_is_not: Not reporting. FP&A is forward-looking and partnership-based; reporting is backward-looking and produced on a schedule.
whats_hard: You must tell a business head their plan is unrealistic while depending on them for the inputs.
not_for_you_if: You avoid confrontation. Useful FP&A is politely adversarial.
demand_note: Strong demand in GCCs and Indian SaaS. Well-defined career ladder to CFO.

title: Investment Banking Analyst
one_line: Builds the models and books behind M&A, fundraising and IPOs. The hours are the reputation.
what_they_do: Produces valuation models, pitch books, information memoranda and financial analysis for transactions. Supports senior bankers on live deals and pitches. Extremely high volume of precise, deadline-driven work.
typical_week: Build or update an operating model and a valuation
Produce a comparable companies and precedent transactions analysis
Turn a model into a pitch book slide
Populate or manage a data room
Turn a comment sheet at 1am and again at 4am
what_it_is_not: Not investment management. Bankers advise on transactions and earn fees; investors deploy capital and earn returns.
entry_paths: From transaction advisory or Big Four
Boutique bank as a first step
whats_hard: The hours are genuinely severe and the work is not intellectually difficult so much as relentlessly precise under deadline.
not_for_you_if: You need predictable hours or protected personal time in the first few years.
demand_note: Highly competitive entry. Boutique and mid-market firms are the realistic route for most PGDM graduates.

title: Venture Capital Analyst
one_line: Evaluates startups. Mostly reading, meeting and judging, not modelling.
what_they_do: Sources and screens startups, runs early diligence on market, team and traction, builds the investment note, and supports portfolio companies afterwards. The financial modelling is lighter than in banking; the judgement is heavier.
typical_week: Meet five or six founders and write them up
Build a bottom-up market size for a sector nobody has data on
Analyse a startup's unit economics and find the assumption that carries everything
Write an investment memo and defend it in partner meeting
Help a portfolio company with a hiring or metrics problem
what_it_is_not: Not private equity. VC underwrites growth in companies with little history; PE underwrites cash flows in companies with a lot.
skills_myth: An MBA from a top school
entry_paths: From an accelerator or angel network
whats_hard: You are wrong most of the time by design, feedback arrives years later, and entry is heavily network-dependent.
not_for_you_if: You need to know whether your decisions were right within a reasonable timeframe.
demand_note: Small number of positions, very high interest. Startup operating experience often beats a finance degree.

title: Private Equity Analyst
one_line: Underwrites control investments in companies with real cash flows.
what_they_do: Models leveraged buyouts, runs deep diligence, and works with portfolio company management on value creation. Heavier modelling and more operational involvement than VC.
typical_week: Build or stress an LBO model
Coordinate diligence workstreams across advisers
Analyse a target's quality of earnings
Prepare an investment committee paper
Review a portfolio company's monthly performance
what_it_is_not: Not VC. PE buys control of profitable businesses and improves them; VC buys minority stakes in unprofitable ones and backs growth.
entry_paths: From investment banking, usually after two to three years
whats_hard: Almost never a first job. The standard path runs through banking or Big Four transaction services first.
not_for_you_if: You are looking for a direct entry route from a PGDM. It rarely exists.
demand_note: Concentrated in Mumbai and Bengaluru. Small, competitive, largely lateral hiring.

title: Equity Research Analyst
one_line: Covers a set of companies deeply and publishes a view with a number attached.
what_they_do: Builds and maintains models for companies in one sector, tracks results and management commentary, and publishes reports with a rating and target price. Accountable for a public, dated, checkable opinion.
typical_week: Update a model after a quarterly result
Listen to an earnings call and note what management avoided
Write a note with a defensible target price
Speak to institutional clients about the sector
Revise a thesis that is not playing out
what_it_is_not: Not portfolio management. Research produces the view; the fund manager takes the risk.
whats_hard: Your view is public, timestamped and checkable. Being wrong is visible in a way it is not in most finance roles.
not_for_you_if: You dislike writing. The report is the product.
demand_note: Large Indian research KPO industry serving global banks is a common entry route.

title: Transaction Advisory Analyst
one_line: Does the financial diligence that decides whether a deal happens at that price.
what_they_do: Analyses a target's historical financials for a buyer — quality of earnings, working capital normalisation, one-off items, debt-like items. Produces the report the buyer prices from.
typical_week: Analyse three years of a target's monthly financials
Normalise working capital and identify one-offs
Question management on a revenue recognition policy
Draft findings that will change the purchase price
Coordinate with legal and commercial diligence teams
what_it_is_not: Not audit. Audit gives an opinion on whether statements are fairly stated; diligence asks what the earnings are actually worth to a buyer.
skills_myth: It is a stepping stone only
entry_paths: From audit into Big Four TAS
whats_hard: You work to a deal timetable on incomplete information, and your findings can kill something a lot of people want to happen.
not_for_you_if: You need a stable schedule. Deal cycles do not respect one.
demand_note: Big Four TAS teams hire in volume in India. One of the strongest routes toward PE.

title: Startup Finance Lead / CFO
one_line: The only finance person, doing every finance job at once.
what_they_do: Owns everything financial in a small company — accounting oversight, cash runway, fundraising support, board reporting, compliance, and the operating model. Breadth over depth, and the runway calculation is the job that matters most.
typical_week: Update the runway and cash forecast
Prepare the board pack
Support a fundraise — data room, model, diligence questions
Handle a compliance or tax matter
Tell a founder something is unaffordable
what_it_is_not: Not a corporate CFO role. There is no team, no systems and no precedent — you build all three while running the function.
entry_paths: From CA practice with startup clients
whats_hard: You are the person who has to say the runway is nine months, not eighteen. Being right and unwelcome is the recurring position.
not_for_you_if: You want deep specialisation. This is the broadest finance role there is.
demand_note: Growing with the Indian startup ecosystem. Fractional and part-time versions increasingly common.

title: Credit / Risk Analyst
one_line: Decides whether to lend, how much, and at what price.
what_they_do: Assesses a borrower's ability to repay — financials, cash flows, collateral, sector risk — and writes the credit note that a committee approves or declines. In market risk roles, measures and limits exposure instead.
typical_week: Spread a borrower's financials and analyse cash flow coverage
Write a credit appraisal note with a recommendation
Present to a credit committee and defend it
Monitor an existing exposure for early warning signals
Update a risk model or a limit
what_it_is_not: Not sales. Relationship managers bring the deal; credit decides whether the bank takes it.
whats_hard: You are rewarded for saying no correctly and blamed for saying no unnecessarily, and both are hard to prove.
not_for_you_if: You want to be liked by the commercial side of the business.
demand_note: Very large hiring across Indian banks, NBFCs and fintech lenders.

title: Treasury Analyst
one_line: Makes sure the money is in the right place, in the right currency, at the right time.
what_they_do: Manages cash positioning, liquidity, short-term investments, banking relationships and FX or interest rate exposure. Highly operational with real deadlines every day.
typical_week: Position cash across accounts and entities
Forecast short-term liquidity
Execute or monitor an FX hedge
Manage a banking relationship or facility
Reconcile and report the daily position
what_it_is_not: Not accounting or FP&A. Treasury deals with actual money movement rather than its recording or projection.
whats_hard: Daily deadlines that cannot slip, and errors are immediately expensive and visible.
not_for_you_if: You prefer project work to daily operational rhythm.
demand_note: Steady demand in large corporates, GCCs and shared service centres.

title: Investment / Portfolio Manager
one_line: Takes the risk. Everyone else in finance advises; this role decides.
what_they_do: Constructs and manages a portfolio against a mandate and a benchmark, sizing positions and managing risk. In wealth management, does the same for individual clients with their goals and constraints.
typical_week: Review positions against the mandate and risk limits
Meet analysts and challenge their theses
Size or exit a position
Report performance and attribution
Explain underperformance to clients or a committee
what_it_is_not: Not equity research. Research recommends; the manager owns the decision and the outcome.
entry_paths: From analyst roles inside a fund
Wealth management route with client focus
whats_hard: Performance is public, measured continuously against a benchmark, and largely determined by factors you do not control.
not_for_you_if: You cannot sit with being wrong in public for extended periods.
demand_note: Small, senior, almost never an entry role. Wealth management is the accessible entry point.
